::: {.graph-container}
```{r}
#| label: plot-hard-hit-vs-barrels
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
library(htmltools)

# 1. Load Statcast hitter data
statcast_hitters <- read_csv("data/statcast_hitters.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
names(statcast_hitters)[1] <- "player_name"

# Helper to normalize player names for joining with Lahman
clean_hitter_name <- function(x) {
  has_comma <- grepl(",", x)
  x[has_comma] <- paste(sub("^.*,\\s*", "", x[has_comma]), sub(",.*$", "", x[has_comma]))
  x <- iconv(x, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")
  x <- gsub("['\"`^~.]", "", x)
  x <- gsub("\\s+(Jr|Sr|II|III|IV)$", "", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- stringr::str_squish(x)
  x <- tolower(x)
  gsub("\\b([a-z])\\s+([a-z])\\b", "\\1\\2", x)
}

# 2. Get franchise name mappings from Lahman
teams_map <- Lahman::Teams |>
  group_by(franchID) |>
  slice_max(yearID, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(franchID, team_name = name) |>
  mutate(team_name = case_when(
    franchID == "ANA" ~ "Los Angeles Angels",
    franchID == "OAK" ~ "Oakland Athletics",
    franchID == "FLA" ~ "Miami Marlins",
    franchID == "TBD" ~ "Tampa Bay Rays",
    franchID == "WSN" ~ "Washington Nationals",
    TRUE ~ team_name
  ))

# 3. Match each hitter to their team for that season
hitter_teams <- Lahman::Batting |>
  filter(yearID >= 2015) |>
  group_by(playerID, yearID) |>
  slice_max(AB, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(Lahman::People |> select(playerID, nameFirst, nameLast), by = "playerID") |>
  mutate(cname = clean_hitter_name(paste(nameFirst, nameLast))) |>
  select(cname, year = yearID, teamID) |>
  distinct(cname, year, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  left_join(
    Lahman::Teams |> select(yearID, teamID, franchID) |> distinct(),
    by = c("year" = "yearID", "teamID")
  ) |>
  left_join(teams_map, by = "franchID") |>
  select(cname, year, team_name)

# 4. Prepare combined hitter dataset with qualified batted balls
hitters_clean <- statcast_hitters |>
  filter(attempts >= 100) |>
  mutate(
    clean_name = if_else(
      grepl(",", player_name),
      paste(sub("^.*,\\s*", "", player_name), sub(",.*$", "", player_name)),
      player_name
    ),
    cname = clean_hitter_name(player_name)
  ) |>
  left_join(hitter_teams, by = c("cname", "year")) |>
  mutate(
    team_name = replace_na(team_name, "Other / Multi-Team"),
    year = factor(year, levels = as.character(2025:2015))
  )

# 5. SharedData handle for coordinated client-side filtering
sd <- SharedData$new(hitters_clean)

# 6. Build interactive scatter plot
p <- plot_ly(
  data = sd,
  x = ~ev95percent,
  y = ~brl_percent,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(
    size = 8,
    color = ~avg_hit_speed,
    colorscale = "Viridis",
    showscale = TRUE,
    colorbar = list(title = "Avg EV<br>(mph)"),
    line = list(color = "#333333", width = 0.5),
    opacity = 0.85
  ),
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>", clean_name, "</b> (", year, ")<br>",
    "Team: ", team_name, "<br>",
    "Hard-Hit Rate (95+ mph): ", ev95percent, "%<br>",
    "Barrel Rate: ", brl_percent, "%<br>",
    "Avg Exit Velocity: ", avg_hit_speed, " mph"
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text",
  height = 460
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "<b>Why 95+ MPH Matters: Hard-Hit Rate vs. Barrel Rate</b><br><sup>Hitters who hit the ball 95+ mph most often produce the highest percentage of barrels</sup>",
      font = list(size = 13)
    ),
    xaxis = list(title = "Hard-Hit Rate (% of batted balls >= 95 mph)", zeroline = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Barrel Rate (% optimal EV & launch angle)", zeroline = FALSE),
    margin = list(t = 60, b = 50, l = 50, r = 40)
  )

# 7. Render side-by-side dropdown selectors and chart
tagList(
  bscols(
    widths = c(6, 6),
    filter_select("filter_year", "Select Season:", sd, ~year),
    filter_select("filter_team", "Select Team:", sd, ~team_name)
  ),
  p
)
```
:::

Understanding the metrics used throughout this analysis helps clarify how Major League Baseball has evolved. Here is what each statistic measures and why it matters in modern baseball.

## Strikeouts per 9 Innings (K/9)

- **What it is:** The average number of strikeouts a pitcher records for every 9 innings pitched.
$$\text{K/9} = \frac{\text{Strikeouts} \times 9}{\text{Innings Pitched}}$$
- **Why it matters:** Strikeouts are the purest measure of pitching dominance because they take the defense and ballpark dimensions out of the equation. As pitchers gained access to pitch-tracking data, league-wide K/9 rose significantly.

## Hard-Hit Percentage (Hard-Hit %)

- **What it is:** The proportion of batted balls hit with an exit velocity of **95 mph or greater**.
$$\text{Hard-Hit \%} = \frac{\text{Batted Balls with Exit Velocity} \ge 95\text{ mph}}{\text{Total Batted Balls}} \times 100$$
- **Pre-Statcast vs. Statcast measurement:**
  - **Pre-Statcast (2005–2014):** Tracked by Baseball Info Solutions (BIS) scouts manually classifying contact into soft, medium, or hard trajectories through video analysis.
  - **Statcast Era (2015–Present):** Tracked automatically using radar and high-speed cameras to record exact exit velocities.
- **Why it matters:** Exit velocity is the strongest predictor of offensive success. Balls struck at 95+ mph produce the vast majority of extra-base hits and home runs.

## Whiff Rate

- **What it is:** The percentage of total swings where a batter swings and misses completely.
$$\text{Whiff Rate} = \frac{\text{Swings and Misses}}{\text{Total Swings}} \times 100$$
- **Why it matters:** Unlike batting average or overall contact, whiff rate pinpoints a batter's vulnerability against specific pitch types and zone locations—such as high fastballs or low breaking balls outside the zone.

## The Statcast Context

Prior to 2015, player evaluation relied on box-score results and scout observation. The introduction of Statcast in all 30 MLB stadiums equipped teams with automated optical cameras and radar to track:

1. **Pitch movement & spin rate:** Helping pitchers design sharper, higher-rising fastballs that create more swings and misses.
2. **Batted-ball trajectories (exit velocity & launch angle):** Helping hitters optimize their swing paths to elevate balls with high exit velocities.

This data revolution explains why the league migrated diagonally toward higher strikeouts and harder-hit balls at the same time.

## Learn More

For full definitions and further reading on every tracking metric, explore the official [MLB Statcast Glossary](https://www.mlb.com/glossary/statcast).
